text: The Active Customer term is approved. Now we make it enforceable: three data quality rules with a threshold and a named owner notified the moment each one fails.

Oracle's own Customer ID must be non-null and unique, full stop. Customer Status must match the approved Active Customer definition exactly. Net Revenue must be non-negative, unless a documented credit explains why it isn't.
This checks the data against the glossary term itself. A row flagged active without a qualifying invoice is a governance defect, routed straight to the Financial domain's named owners.
A flat non-negative rule would fail every real credit, so this allows a negative line only with a documented reason code -- with a small tolerance for a known legacy backlog.
The definitions are enforced. Next: who can see the sensitive data underneath them, and a report proving the program still holds up.
